facts.raw_span: 5-year history of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque
no previous history of trauma or any other systemic symptoms
nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
No local lymphadenopathy was observed
Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV: Negative
Hepatitis B: Negative
Hepatitis C: Negative
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Perls Prussian blue staining showed prominent hemosiderin deposits

concepts.why: The patient's lesion is consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, given the presence of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, and the poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation.

The patient's lesion is also consistent with hemangioma, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis and prominent hemosiderin deposits.

The patient's lesion is also consistent with vascular malformation, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque and poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with dermatofibroma, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with cherry angioma, given the presence of a reddish-brown annular plaque.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with pyogenic granuloma, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque.

The patient's lesion is also consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis and prominent hemosiderin deposits.

The patient's lesion is also consistent with spindle cell hemangioma, given the presence of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, and the poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with verrucous hemangioma, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque.
The patient's lesion is also consistent with angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia, given the presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque.

The presence of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation and small dilated, cleftlike, irregular, thin-walled vascular channels dissecting collagen bundles, along with the negative staining for HHV-8, is consistent with hobnail hemangioma.

rationales.F05: The presence of CD31, CD34, and D2-40 positivity in vascular channel endothelial cells is more typical of a benign vascular lesion, such as hemangioma or vascular malformation.
rationales.F06: The absence of HHV-8 and WT1 negativity is more typical of a benign vascular lesion, such as hemangioma or vascular malformation, rather than Kaposi's sarcoma.
rationales.F11: The poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation is more typical of a benign vascular lesion, such as hemangioma or vascular malformation.
rationales.F12: The presence of prominent hemosiderin deposits is more typical of a targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
